newsitem.title: FRANCE: Blast hits French premier Juppe's mayoral office.
newsitem.headline: Blast hits French premier Juppe's mayoral office.

text.p: A strong blast damaged the mayoral offices of Prime Minister Alain Juppe in Bordeaux in southwestern France overnight, causing damage but no casualties, officials said on Sunday.

The explosion shortly before midnight (2200 GMT Saturday) shattered windows in a hall of the elegant building, which the centre-right premier had left several hours previously on Saturday afternoon, the fire brigade said.
Police said the blast had probably been caused by a bomb placed at ground level beneath the windows of the ornate reception rooms.
Bernard Fragneau, government representative (prefect) in charge of security, told reporters that the explosion had apparently happened outside the building.
Asked whether the blast was caused by a bomb or by a gas leak, Fragneau said he could not comment but that as far as he knew there was no gas outlet at the site of the explosion.
Juppe, who took office as prime minister early last year, regularly visits the port city but he does not reside at the city hall.
Public prosecutor Patrice Davost visited the scene, which was sealed off by police who searched through the upper floors of the building.
